images.title: A milestone, a hop and a hop back
images.purpose: Show that adding 98 is the same as adding 100 and taking 2 back.
images.composition: A road from the milestone 54 with a long hop of 100 to the milestone 154 and a short hop back of 2 to the milestone 152.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. A road with three milestones and two hops (the road is not to scale). The road is a thick construction grey #6B7280 horizontal line (16 px) from x 100 to x 1356 at y 450. THREE MILESTONES stand on the road, each a rounded-top stone 100 by 80 px (y 370 to 450), filled white, outlined dark #2B2B2B 3 px, holding in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px) a number: 54 at x 150 to 250, 152 at x 950 to 1050 and 154 at x 1110 to 1210. A long hop: a curved arrow in teal #0072B2 (6 px) above the road from the top of the milestone 54 (x 200, y 370) to the top of the milestone 154 (x 1160, y 370), peaking at y 240, with the label +100 in teal bold (72 px) centred at x 680, y 190. A short hop back: a curved arrow in amber #E69F00 (6 px) below the road from x 1160 to x 1000, y 468, dipping to y 600, with the label −2 in amber bold (64 px) centred at x 1080, y 655. At the top left, x 120, y 90, the caption 98 is 2 less than 100 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). At the bottom, centred at x 728, y 760, the line 54 + 98 = 152 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (84 px). No other text. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Add the round number, then take the extra back: 54 + 100 − 2 = 152.
images.description: A road with milestones 54, 152 and 154, a hop of +100 and a hop back of −2.
images.context: Concept image for Near-Round Numbers: Add, Then Take Back, using the example's own numbers (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Say why 2 are taken back: the 98 was 2 less than 100. The slip to watch: stopping at 154.

image_decisions.why: The picture is the mathematics: the long hop to the round number and the short hop back are the easier way.
